claim_text: Kurly says an outside attacker stole login credentials and used them to get into its work systems on Nov 17
summary: In a Nov 20 apology notice, Kurly said an outside attacker reached its systems by 'abnormal means' on Nov 17, stole login credentials and used them to enter internal work systems. It reported the breach to the authorities on Nov 18.
detail: This is Kurly's own account. We read the notice's full text as reprinted by one outlet, not on Kurly's site, which did not load for us, so it is counted as one company statement. Yonhap, Chosunbiz, SBS, KBS and others repeat it and add no separate confirmation. No outside party has checked it. Kurly has not said how the credentials were stolen.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The company itself says it was attacked from outside and data was taken; no outside source has confirmed or contradicted it.
notes: Company admission relayed. Upgrade to Confirmed if the notice is read on kurly.com or a regulator confirms.

summary: Kurly says the names, user IDs, phone numbers, email addresses and social media channel details of 10,699 curators were leaked.
detail: Curators are not delivery staff. They are people who promote Kurly products on their own social media and get a fee when a purchase follows their link. The number and the data types are Kurly's own figures.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Kurly's notice lists the data types and the count; no outside source has seen the data.
notes: Sweep notes called them delivery partners; sources say affiliate promoters.

claim_text: Some curators' bank account and resident or business registration numbers were included
summary: Kurly says that for some curators, bank account numbers and resident registration numbers or business registration numbers were also leaked.
detail: Kurly has not said how many curators this covers. One outlet (Ajupress) notes the number is undisclosed. Another (Alpha Economy) reports that Kurly's notice does not say whether the ID numbers were stored encrypted. We could not re-read that article, which blocks automated access.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Kurly's notice says some curators' bank and ID numbers were included but gives no count.
notes: Do not repeat figures for ID-number victims; none published.

claim_text: Names, departments and email addresses of 199 current and former employees were also leaked
summary: On Nov 23, after checking all documents accessed over the weekend, Kurly said 199 employees, including former ones, had their names, department names and email addresses leaked, and began notifying them from 9 AM KST.
detail: Kurly says phone numbers, addresses, passwords and payment details were not included. This came from a statement to the press, not a notice we could read in full.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Kurly's Nov 23 statement, relayed by several outlets, gives the number and data types.
notes: One statement, counted as one source.

claim_text: Four ordinary customers were affected, not the whole customer base
summary: Kurly said on Nov 20 that two customers' member numbers leaked, and on Nov 23 that two more customers' anonymous user IDs (UUIDs) and usage records were exposed: four in all.
detail: Kurly says names, phone numbers, addresses, passwords and payment details were not exposed and that it does not collect ordinary customers' resident ID or bank details. EBN totals the people affected at 10,902. Yonhap's Nov 23 piece reads as if only the first two customers were affected, but the Nov 23 statement as reported by Chosunbiz, EBN and Sports Donga adds two more.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Kurly's two statements give two customers each time; outlets total four.
notes: Earlier sweep note said only 2; updated.

claim_text: Who the attacker was and how the login credentials were stolen
summary: Neither Kurly nor any outlet we read names a group or describes how the credentials were taken. Kurly says it will investigate the cause.
detail: Kurly calls the intruder an 'external attacker'. No ransom note, group claim or sale of the data is reported. We did not look at leak or dark-web sites.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Nothing in the notice or the coverage identifies the attacker or the method.

claim_text: Kurly reported the breach to the authorities on Nov 18
summary: Kurly says it reported the breach to the relevant authorities on Nov 18, the day after the attack, and told them again about the added victims on Nov 23.
detail: Kurly does not name the authority in what we read. Coverage says 'relevant authorities'.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Kurly's own notice says so; no agency has confirmed receiving it.

claim_text: Kurly will give affected curators 50,000 to 150,000 won in app credit and says it will pay full damages
summary: Kurly says affected curators will get 50,000 to 150,000 won in Kurly app credit depending on what leaked, usable within a year, and that it will compensate any actual loss in full.
detail: Alpha Economy points out the credit can only be spent on Kurly. That article could not be re-read. Kurly says employees and customers will also be compensated if harm is shown.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The offer is in Kurly's notice and relayed by outlets.

claim_text: Whether the stolen data is circulating or has been misused
summary: Kurly says it is checking whether the data is circulating outside and will ask the authorities to help remove it. No outlet reports misuse.
detail: One outlet notes that no secondary crime using the data has been confirmed. We did not search leak sites.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Kurly says it is monitoring; no source reports the data published or used.

claim_text: The privacy regulator's or the internet agency's response
summary: We found no public statement from Korea's privacy regulator (PIPC) or the internet security agency (KISA) about this breach.
detail: Coverage says only that Kurly reported to 'relevant authorities'. Revisit on any PIPC announcement of an investigation or penalty.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No agency statement exists in what we read; Kurly's report to authorities is the only trace.
notes: Checked Nov 23 via web search only.
